findings.title: Repeated counterparties are visible
findings.body: 68 transfers connect this wallet and 0x6adb…c200 in this sample window. This establishes an on-chain connection, not a personal relationship.
findings.method: Group successful ETH transfers by counterparty address. Minimum: 3 transfers.

findings.title: Transaction times form a public pattern
findings.body: 20 of 100 transfers occurred between 09:00 and 12:00 UTC. Automation and counterparties can determine these times; they do not establish your timezone.
findings.method: Count timestamps in eight fixed 3-hour UTC buckets; report the largest. No location inference.

findings.title: Who owns this wallet?
findings.body: Not established. Public transfer data does not identify the person controlling an address.
findings.method: No identity, purpose, or location evidence is collected.

findings.title: What were these payments for?
findings.body: Not established. Similar amounts and intervals do not identify salary, rent, purchases, or self-transfers.
findings.method: No identity, purpose, or location evidence is collected.

findings.title: Where does the owner live?
findings.body: Not established. UTC activity patterns are not reliable evidence of a person’s location.
findings.method: No identity, purpose, or location evidence is collected.

limitations: An address does not establish a person, employer, salary, location, or payment purpose.
Only successful, positive-value, normal ETH transactions are analyzed. Token transfers, internal calls, fees, other chains, and zero-value interactions are excluded.
One counterparty can represent many people. Several addresses can belong to one person. This report does not resolve ownership.
The live report uses at most the latest 100 normal transactions, filtered to the selected period. It is not a complete wallet history.
